items.item: One integrated system in which a sales order can automatically: check available stock, reserve inventory, calculate shortages, generate production plans, raise purchase requirements, manage job work vendors, track the complete manufacturing lifecycle
items.evidence: Automatic on confirmation: POST /sales/{id}/confirm (apps/api/src/modules/sales/router.py:224, sales_order.update) calls sales.service.confirm_order (service.py:1608). It runs the credit check (assert_customer_can_order), reads live AvailabilityRepository.available_by_item, reserves min(demand, available) through AllocationPort, and returns the shortfall per line (LineAllocationRead.shortfall_quantity, schemas.py:305-376; GET /sales/{id}/allocation-status, router.py:292). UI: sales-order-detail-page.tsx:353 (confirm) and :216-220 (a 'Run MRP to plan the balance' link). Planning: POST /mrp/runs (mrp/router.py:142, mrp.run) calls start_run (mrp/service.py:459), which reads the open sales-order book (_collect_demand :413). A run executes inline at 50 demand lines or fewer (core/config.py:261), otherwise on Celery queue 'mrp' (:595). It produces MANUFACTURE, PURCHASE and JOB_WORK suggestions (mrp/models.py:129-142). POST /mrp/suggestions/{id}/convert (router.py:350) turns a suggestion into a document through CONVERSION_HOOKS (service.py:208-221): production.create_order_from_mrp (production/service.py:1219) or procurement.create_requisition_from_mrp (procurement/service.py:572). job_work.create_order_from_mrp (job_work/service.py:2502) refuses by design. The UI converts in bulk at mrp-run-detail-page.tsx:368-372. Job-work and production lifecycle modules exist (/job-work, /production, /production/work-orders).
items.gap: Production plans and purchase requirements are not raised automatically from the sales order. Nothing in sales/service.py references MRP, and celery_app.py beat_schedule has no MRP entry, so a planner must start a run and then convert its suggestions. JOB_WORK suggestions cannot be converted at all. There is no lifecycle view centred on the sales order: production orders created by MRP store source_type=MRP_SUGGESTION and source_id=<suggestion id> (production/models.py:124-134), not the sales order, and the order detail page lists no linked production, job-work, packing or dispatch documents. In the base and dev compose files the worker has no -Q (docker-compose.yml:250, docker-compose.dev.yml:66), so asynchronous MRP runs (over 50 lines) never execute outside the prod overlay.
items.planned_wp: None covers the automation or the order-level trace. A2 only fixes the dev worker queue; B4 only adds a 'Production shortage' notification after a run.
items.recommendation: Medium. (1) Add a company setting auto_plan_on_confirm. When it is on and a confirmed order is short, enqueue one MRP run per company after commit, coalescing bursts and reusing start_run, the planning lock and RateLimitPolicy.MRP_RUN. (2) Add a Celery beat task mrp.scheduled_run (nightly, per active company, switched by a setting). (3) Add an optional, audited auto-convert policy: PURCHASE to a DRAFT requisition, MANUFACTURE to a DRAFT production order, never a purchase order. (4) Add GET /sales/{id}/fulfilment (sales_order.view), batched through ports, returning reservations, MRP suggestions whose source_demands reference the order's lines, production orders, requisitions and POs, job-work orders, packing orders and dispatches. Show it as a Fulfilment panel on the order detail page, and persist sales_order_id/sales_order_line_id on MRP-created production orders and requisition lines.

items.item: Conclusion: 12 most important modules (Inventory Engine, Multi-role Item Master, Multi-level BOM, Common Parts Calculation, Allocation & Reallocation, MRP Planning, Production Management, Assembly Line, Job Work, Quality Control, Packing & Dispatch, Finance & Reports)
items.evidence:
All 12 exist on main with routes and screens:
- Inventory: 33 routes; /inventory, /inventory/ledger, /reservations, /movements.
- Multi-role item master: 9 can_* flags (products/models.py:396-422), edited in item-form-dialog.tsx.
- Multi-level BOM: 14 routes, with versions, approval and costing.
- Common parts: GET /bom/{id}/explode consolidates (bom/router.py:294), and MRP merges common parts.
- Allocation and reallocation: allocation router.
- MRP: 10 routes.
- Production: 27 routes, including work orders.
- Assembly: 16 routes. Job work: 16. QC: 15. Packing: 21. Dispatch: 14.
- Finance router and reports (22 routes).
items.gap:
Three modules have gaps:
- Finance has no sales invoices, credit notes or receivable follow-up.
- Allocation and reallocation cannot approve a reallocation in the UI (see S01.2).
- MRP produces no TRANSFER or reallocation suggestions (the docstring at mrp/models.py:132-136 says TRANSFER is not produced).
items.planned_wp: Finance: A2, A3, A4. Job-work invoice: B3a. Shift planning: B2. Not covered: the reallocation approval screen and MRP transfer/reallocation suggestions.
items.recommendation: Small: the reallocation approval UI (see S01.2). Medium: an MRP pass that, before falling back to MANUFACTURE or PURCHASE, proposes a TRANSFER from free stock in other warehouses and a REALLOCATION from lower-priority soft reservations, feeding the existing reallocation-request API (cross-reference P06.O4/O5 and K10).

notes:
Scope and baseline. This is a read-only audit of the main tree C:\Project\Other\ATCRAFT at HEAD cdac4e0, which was unchanged throughout. No round-1 lane (A1, B1, C0) is merged, so every status describes main. Paths in the evidence are relative to the repository root.

Planned work packages. SPEC-INDEX gained D1–D5 during the audit. D5-specifications-accessories (R3/B) closes the 'specification masters' and 'accessories' gaps (S02.4, S02.5). C3a was revised at 17:08 to consume D5's batch helpers.

1. Dev and base worker queue defect (affects S01.1 and S02.9). The celery-worker in docker-compose.yml:250 and docker-compose.dev.yml:66, and the Makefile/make.ps1 dev-worker targets, run without -Q. celery_app.py routes mrp.* to 'mrp' and reports.* to 'reports', so in the dev stack these never execute:
   - MRP runs above 50 demand lines;
   - every PDF/XLSX job (packing list, large reports, valuation export).
   Only docker-compose.prod.yml:83 subscribes to those queues. A2 fixes this. Until then, a final e2e run on the dev stack will hang on PDFs and on large MRP runs.

2. Gaps in my sections that no work package covers:
   - (a) S01.1: SO confirmation never triggers MRP; there is no scheduled MRP run and no sales-order fulfilment/trace view.
   - (b) S01.2/N10: reallocation requests can be raised but never approved or rejected in the UI. The API exists at allocation/router.py:212-297. The generic /audit/approvals decide endpoints are also unused by the SPA. This also blocks P05.S6 and K05.
   - (c) S02.3/S02.5: no variant create/edit screen.
   - (d) S02.3/S02.6: the item form cannot edit sale_price/dealer_price (also relevant to P04.M9/M10).
   - (e) S02.6: manual SO line discounts are ungated and never trigger approval. The below-cost check uses the price before discount.
   - (f) S02.3: no editor for item-vendor links (also relevant to P07 and preferred-vendor-driven PO creation).
   - (g) S02.14: results of 5,000 rows or fewer cannot be exported, and no report has a PDF export.
   - (h) S02.14: PRODUCT_PROFITABILITY exposes standard cost to anyone with report.view.
   - (i) S02.2: address and contact writes on dealer accounts bypass the dealer.manage rule.
   - (j) N10: MRP never produces TRANSFER or REALLOCATION suggestions (P06.O4/O5, K10).

3. Notifications. Only 4 of the 20 NotificationType members are emitted on main: DISPATCH_DELAYED, ALLOCATION_CHANGED, QC_FAILED and REPORT_READY. B4, C1a and A5 cover the rest. Auditors for A01/A08 should verify against this list.

4. Sales lifecycle. SalesOrderStatus INVOICED and CLOSED are unreachable on main (no caller). A2 closes this.

5. Mobile API (S02.15). It is planned as a PWA inside the same SPA (C3a/C4a). The refresh token is only in an HttpOnly cookie with X-CSRF-Token (assumptions §14), so a native app would need a cookie jar. Confirm with the client whether any native app must keep working.

6. Handover (N09). The repository has no git remote; plan the source handover mechanism.

items.item: Security and technical improvements required before production-ready
items.evidence: All P01 controls are present (see P01.*). On main, vendor-portal principals are not data-isolated: every vendor role holds DISPATCH_VIEW and DOCUMENT_VIEW (_VENDOR_BASE, API/core/permissions.py:451-458), and owner/account roles add VENDOR_INVOICE_VIEW, PAYMENT_VIEW, LEDGER_VIEW, JOB_WORK_VIEW, QC_VIEW (:612-675), while dispatch, finance, job_work, quality and documents repositories apply no tenant.vendor_id predicate (vendor scoping exists only in procurement/repository.py:675,908,1216,1320, users and products) and API/core/deps.py has no global vendor gate (forbid_vendor_users is used on 2 procurement routes). docs/security.md section 4 claims vendor users 'are scoped to their own vendor's records'; tests/api/test_vendor_portal_scope_http.py covers purchase orders only.
items.gap: A vendor user can list the company's dispatches, documents, other vendors' invoices/payments, the ledger, job-work orders and QC inspections (by code reading).

notes:
Read-only audit of main at cdac4e0 (apps/api/src, apps/web/src, docs). Nothing was executed; defects marked 'found by reading' are unverified at runtime and no existing test covers them.

Totals: P03 = 20 PRESENT, 9 PARTIAL, 1 PLANNED_FULL (T9 via A3). P05 = 12 PRESENT, 17 PARTIAL, 2 PLANNED_PARTIAL (S6, S9 via B4), 2 ABSENT (D1, D5); P03.F8 is PLANNED_PARTIAL via B4. Only A3 (return stock) and B4 (approver notification + link fix) touch these sections; everything else here is unplanned.

Cross-cutting findings:
1. Allocation has no back-channel to the demand documents. Sales lines, job-work lines and assembly components keep reservation_id/allocated_quantity. A manual Release on /inventory/reservations, an expiry, or a reallocation leaves them stale. Their own release paths then call allocation.release on a closed reservation, which raises (allocation/service.py:376-399). Result: a sales order can no longer be dispatched, cancelled or edited.
2. Reallocation does not work end to end:
   - There is no approval screen, so ALLOCATION_APPROVE is unused in apps/web (the handbook says so too).
   - The recipient reservation has demand_line_id=None, so dispatch and production issue never consume it.
   - The urgent sales order stays CONFIRMED and dispatch refuses it.
   - A demand with zero reservation cannot start a request from the UI. That is exactly the proposal's 'urgent order vs production' scenario.
3. MRP explodes only directly demanded items, with one consolidated multi-level BOM explosion (mrp/engine.py:1071-1086). So stock of an assembly, semi-finished item or manufactured component does not reduce the demand beneath it. The P05 priority order FG -> assembly -> SFG -> components -> RM holds only at the FG level. This also matters for P06/P04.CON auditors. The TRANSFER suggestion type is never produced, and JOB_WORK suggestions cannot be converted.
4. inventory_balances.allocated_quantity is never written, so the 'Allocated' column on /inventory always shows 0.
5. Priority inputs are inconsistent:
   - Sales order priority is 1-9, but production, assembly, job-work and manual reservations default to 100.
   - is_urgent is unused, and there is no customer priority.
   - Priority/date edits after confirmation are not pushed to reservations.
   - Assembly and job-work reservations carry no priority or date.
6. docs/assumptions.md section 10 (SOFT may be taken without approval) and the handbook do not match the code: every request needs approval, and no module creates SOFT reservations.
7. Traceability and bins:
   - Serial-tracked stock has no user-facing way in; only demo data posts it.
   - Serials and reservations cannot be combined at dispatch.
   - No screen can address a bin, and same-warehouse bin moves are impossible.
8. Endpoints with no screen:
   - transfer cancel/edit
   - adjustment reject/cancel
   - batch/serial create
   - reallocation list/approve/reject
   - assembly create/approve/release
   - physical-count scoping
9. The scrap pool and damaged stock have no disposal path, and scrap is not displayed anywhere.

items.item: MRP flow: Sales Order -> Check FG -> Explode BOM -> Merge -> Check Inventory -> Check Reserved -> Check Incoming PO -> Check Production -> Shortage -> Suggestions
items.evidence: POST /api/v1/mrp/runs [mrp.run] (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/modules/mrp/router.py:142-166) from /mrp 'Run MRP' (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/web/src/features/mrp/mrp-page.tsx:475-560). engine.plan (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/modules/mrp/engine.py:1278-1590): sales orders = open CONFIRMED/ALLOCATED/PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED lines, qty less dispatched less allocated (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/modules/mrp/repository.py:138-200); finished goods = parent netted against free stock and in-time POs before explosion (engine.py:1116-1168); explode (repository.py:487-512 -> BOM engine); merge (engine.py:830-858,995-1019); inventory and reserved = on_hand - reserved - qc_hold - damaged, safety stock held back (engine.py:258-279,460-474); incoming PO = procurement incoming_quantities, time-phased (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/modules/procurement/service.py:3791; engine.py:490-520); production = in_progress_output (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/modules/production/service.py:3407); shortage (engine.py:665-681); suggestions (engine.py:1493-1537).
items.gap: None for the stated flow. Caveats: netting is two-stage, so sub-assembly stock does not reduce its children's demand (P06.F2); open job-work orders are not a supply input (P06.O3).
items.recommendation: See P06.F2 and P06.O3.

Cross-cutting findings, which suggest three work packages:
(1) Item master form gap (small). ItemFormDialog (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/web/src/features/items/item-form-dialog.tsx:63-100) omits fields that the API accepts and that planning depends on: sale_price, dealer_price, default_warehouse_id, min_order_quantity, safety_stock, reorder_quantity, shelf_life_days and the batch/serial flags. Item-vendor links can be listed but not created or edited, and variants cannot be created or edited at all. Fixing these closes P04.M7, M9 and M10, most of P06.F5, and the conversion trap below.
(2) BOM draft editor (medium). PATCH /api/v1/bom/{bom_id} has no screen. This blocks versioning with changes (B4), fixing a draft after rejection (B5), entering BOM operations so costing includes operations (B6), and setting substitute lines or line operation_sequence.
(3) MRP depth (medium-large):
- level-by-level netting, so stocked sub-assemblies stop over-ordering their components (F2);
- routing-based manufacture lead time and offsets per level (F6, F7);
- expected availability dates (F8);
- TRANSFER, REALLOCATION and usable JOB_WORK outputs, with job-work output netted as supply (O3, O4, O5);
- an optional scheduled run.
Adding REALLOCATION, or new TRANSFER columns, changes the binding contract in docs/database.md section 6 and needs a CHECK-constraint migration.

Defects found while auditing:
(a) create_item does not run _require_attributes for finish_id, size_id or colour_id (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/modules/products/service.py:1133-1200 versus 1119-1130). The POST route therefore accepts cross-tenant, wrong-kind or retired attribute ids. This is the 'a foreign key to a UUID is not a tenant check' trap from CLAUDE.md, and the fix is small.
(b) Unscoped MRP runs ('All warehouses', the default on /mrp) cannot convert suggestions for items without a default warehouse, and no screen can set one. The guards are at production/service.py:1236-1244 and procurement/service.py:589-597.
(c) Production orders raised from MRP without a bom_id need a default approved BOM at release. BomFormDialog leaves 'default' unchecked by default, and its hint 'the API rejects a second' is inaccurate: approval demotes the previous default instead (bom/service.py:797-824).
(d) The UI offers Convert for JOB_WORK suggestions (mrp-types.ts:79), but the API always refuses them (job_work/service.py:2502-2520).

Operational note: async MRP runs (more than 50 demand lines; mrp_sync_threshold_demand_lines at C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/core/config.py:261) are routed to the 'mrp' Celery queue. The base and dev compose workers consume only 'default' (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/docker-compose.yml:250, C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/docker-compose.dev.yml:66). The prod overlay consumes it (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/docker-compose.prod.yml:83). Until A2's dev fix lands, large runs on the dev stack stay QUEUED.

notes:
Paths are relative to C:\Project\Other\ATCRAFT. The audit is of main at cdac4e0: round 1 is not merged, so C0 is not on main yet.

1. **Trap T7 strands POs after receipt.** The PO state machine is effectively dead after receipt: nothing drives QC_PENDING->QC_COMPLETED, GRN_COMPLETED->INVOICED or INVOICED->PAID, and goods_receipt_lines.qc_status never leaves PENDING. As a result:
   - every QC'd PO is stuck at QC_PENDING;
   - the PO tracking panel shows 'QC pending' permanently;
   - the GRN 'Waiting on QC' filter never clears;
   - QC_PENDING has no cancel or close exit;
   - there is no Close button in the UI for GRN_COMPLETED POs;
   - vendors with such POs can never be retired (vendors/repository.py:55-67 OPEN_PURCHASE_ORDER_STATUSES; vendors/service.py:1047).

   No planned WP fixes this. C1a only derives a display status from inspections and explicitly avoids these PO statuses. This is the largest unplanned gap in A04, and it should become a small dedicated WP:
   - procurement hooks called from quality (QC verdict) and finance (invoice approve/cancel, payment allocate/reverse);
   - the reverse edges those hooks need;
   - a backfill migration;
   - lifecycle meta-tests.

2. **Gaps no WP covers** (candidates for new WPs):
   - P07.M1: read-only requisition detail for approvers. Approval today is blind.
   - P07.M2: RFQ document and sending it to vendors.
   - P07.M3 / A04.2: selected quotation -> PO.
   - P07.M5: draft PO edit UI, Close/Short-close UI, and the duplicate re-check on PATCH.
   - P07.M6: GRN detail and cancel-draft UI.
   - P07.M7 / A04.11-A04.14: status write-back.
   - P07.M8: vendor debit note on purchase return, and a match net of returns.
   - P07.M9: dispute / resolve / cancel UI for vendor invoices. The routes exist with no screen.
   - P07.M13: actual lead-time measurement.
   - P07.V5: transporter <-> vendor link and freight payables.
   - P07.V6: non-stock service procurement.

3. **Duplicate control (A03) on main.** Detection is real but runs only in create_purchase_order (service.py:2101-2133).
   - Merge, increase quantity and cancel are advisory text (procurement-types.ts:474-511, actionable:false).
   - 'Create new with approval' works only for holders of purchase_order.approve. PURCHASE_EXECUTIVE cannot use it.
   - The backend's CANCEL_DUPLICATE means 'cancel the existing order'. That is the opposite of the proposal's 'cancel duplicate request'.
   - D1 (round 5) plus C0 cover all rules and options. Two caveats remain:
     - D1 keeps vendor and warehouse as hard filters, so a same-demand order raised with a different vendor is never flagged. Confirm with the client.
     - Neither WP re-runs the check on PATCH /purchase-orders/{id}.

4. **Security issues found in the audited flows** (all planned):
   - T2: /check-duplicates lets vendor users read other vendors' open lines (C0 §9).
   - T3: assigned_vendor_user_id and the requisition/quotation line ids are unvalidated FKs (C0 §7, §10).
   - Vendor users see DRAFT and PENDING_APPROVAL POs with prices, and land in the staff shell (C0 §11, C2a).
   - Vendor role presets open unscoped dispatch, finance, quality and documents (C1a P0 allow-list).
   - The internal 'Vendor acknowledged' button is gated on purchase_order.update, which vendor roles also hold.

5. **VendorType is classification only.** vendor_type_predicate (vendors/repository.py:608) has no caller, and no picker filters by type, despite the VendorType docstring. All six types exist in the enum, the DB CHECK and the UI. The demo data has no TRANSPORT vendor.

6. **Related observations outside my sections:**
   - GET /procurement/pending-approvals has no UI.
   - GOODS_RECEIPT_POSTED is never raised.
   - Every planned vendor-notification channel (C1a, C1b, D2) targets vendor user accounts only. A vendor without a portal login gets nothing, and no WP e-mails the PO to the vendor master's e-mail address.

notes:
Scope and method: read-only audit of branch main (HEAD cdac4e0). All paths are relative to C:\Project\Other\ATCRAFT. Every claim was checked in code (models, routers, services, frontend features, route table app/router.tsx:308-359, navigation.ts Manufacturing group). Planned coverage was judged against specs B1-cost-centres, B2-shifts, B3a-job-work-invoice and B4-smart-alerts-events. Tally: 16 PRESENT (P08.M1,M3,M4,M5, P08.S1-S8, P09.M2, P10.M1,M2,M5), 15 PARTIAL, 3 PLANNED_FULL (P08.M7, P08.M8, P10.M9), 4 PLANNED_PARTIAL (P08.M6, P08.M9, P10.M4, P10.M10).

Cross-cutting findings:
1. Assembly cannot be operated from the UI. The /assembly screens call only list/detail/components, issue-components and complete. Create, edit, delete, approve, release, start, close, cancel, qc-result and pack exist as permissioned APIs with no screen. Complete needs IN_PROGRESS, which only Start reaches, so a live tenant cannot take one assembly order through. Only demo orders seeded via the service progress. No WP covers this; it is the biggest gap in P09.
2. QC double-path defect for assembly and job work. quality.decide_inspection moves QC_HOLD stock but never calls back the source module. Assembly and job-work have their own qc-result endpoints, which move the same stock again. Assembly orders get stranded in QC_PENDING with no way to close or pack them, and job-work orders stay QC_PENDING unless the separate job-work verdict is used. This is the same class as the CLAUDE.md trap about a status the state machine cannot leave. It also affects P11.T3/T4, so flag it to the P11 auditor. No WP covers it.
3. Tracked items are refused end to end. Production output refuses batch and serial FG (service.py:3013). Assembly refuses batch components and outputs, and serial outputs. Job work refuses both sides. The material-issue UI has no batch picker. The demo's serialised MAKE item DL-900 can only enter stock through an opening movement (demo_data/operations.py:1335-1344).
4. APIs with no screen: GET /production/wip; GET /production/material-issues and /{id}; PATCH and DELETE /production/{id}; CompleteRequest and CloseRequest fields (the UI posts {}); GET /job-work/{id}/challans, /receipts and /reconciliation; GET /job-work/charges; ReceiveRequest is_final, approve_excess_loss, rejection_action and vendor_challan_date; IssueRequest.transporter_id; GET /assembly/ready-for-packing; the assembly lifecycle endpoints in point 1.
5. UI/API mismatches and wrong UI text:
   - Production booking shift allows 32 characters; the API allows 16.
   - Job-work vehicle number allows 32 characters; the API allows 24.
   - RecordProductionDialog's alert and the EntriesPanel empty state say the first booking moves the order to IN_PROCESS. Only Start does that.
   - JobWorkReceiveDialog's alert says the API decides scrap or debit from the order. In fact rejection_action defaults to RETURN_TO_STOCK.
   - Assembly 'Issue components' is offered on COMPONENTS_ISSUED and IN_PROGRESS, but the state machine has no edge for it, so it always fails.
   - The job-work receive prefill is miscomputed.
6. Machine status is never consulted. WORKABLE_MACHINE_STATUSES (routing/repository.py:59) is dead. Production supervisors lack user.view, so every operator picker is empty for them; B2 fixes this.
7. Linkage gaps:
   - Outsourced routing operations (is_outsourced, job_work_vendor_id) do not create or link job-work orders at release.
   - Production cost excludes job-work charges.
   - MRP has no assembly-order target and does not net open assembly orders.
   - MRP refuses to convert JOB_WORK suggestions.
   - Packing never consumes the assembly ready-for-packing feed.
8. Suggested new work packages, none planned today:
   - (a) Assembly completion: lifecycle UI, QC sync, packing handover, Start and partial completion (P09.M1, M3-M7, EX).
   - (b) Job-work operations: order detail and timeline, challan PDF and register, receive options (is_final, excess-loss approval, rejection action), QC sync, rework order, vendor material ledger (P10.M1, M3-M8, M10).
   - (c) Production completion, costing and WIP: complete/close dialogs, tracked-FG output, costing breakdown and variance report, WIP-by-order tab and valuation (P08.M10-M12).
   - (d) Production planning board and capacity load (P08.M2), after B2 lands.
   - Also add to B2 if possible: work-order-level machine overlap warnings (P08.M6) and a company-wide GET /production/entries (P08.M9).

items.gap: The two release paths are not reconciled. Recording the verdict on the job-work screen moves QC_HOLD->AVAILABLE/DAMAGED and completes the order, but leaves the Quality inspection PENDING in /quality indefinitely. If that inspection is later decided, it posts QC_HOLD->AVAILABLE a second time: the post is refused, or it silently releases another lot held at the same item/warehouse/batch grain. Deciding in Quality first never completes the job-work order, because quality has no owner callback, and the job-work verdict then fails for lack of held stock. The job-work verdict also skips the check sheet and offers no rework, hold or scrap.

notes:
I audited main at cdac4e0 (read-only), checked every claim in code, and cross-checked against the handbook notes in C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/docs/handbook/content.json, which independently confirm the UI gaps. All paths are under C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT.

Defects on main that no work package plans to fix, ordered by severity:

1. **Dispatch lines from the UI never carry `sales_order_line_id`** (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/web/src/features/dispatch/dispatch-dialogs.tsx L169-176).
   - Dispatching against a sales order skips `allocation.consume` and the order-line arithmetic (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/modules/dispatch/service.py L1446-1449, L1550-1553).
   - The reservation stays in place and goods leave from free stock; the dispatch is refused if the only stock is the reserved stock.
   - The order line's `dispatched_quantity` never moves, yet the sales order is still walked to PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED.
   - Demo data names the order lines, which is why seeded data looks right.
   - This blocks A2: A2 builds invoice lines and limits from sales-order lines and `dispatched_quantity`. Fix it before or inside A2 (small).

2. **The QC decision never notifies the document that raised the inspection** (`quality.decide_inspection` has no owner callback).
   - Job work has two release paths: the QC-result action on the job-work screen and the inspection in Quality. Using one leaves the other open. Deciding the leftover later double-posts QC_HOLD stock, either refused or silently releasing another lot at the same item/warehouse/batch position.
   - Assembly orders stay stuck in QC_PENDING: no screen calls `/assembly/{id}/qc-result`.
   - The GRN line's QC status and the purchase order's QC_PENDING never advance, so GRN_COMPLETED is unreachable after QC.
   - Fix with one owner-callback port in quality, keyed on the reference type (medium).

3. **QC coverage is partial.**
   - No screen raises an inspection by hand: the POST `/quality/inspections` endpoint has no UI.
   - Production and packing never raise inspections, so In-process and Final QC are API-only stage labels.
   - Decided inspections cannot be opened, so readings and photos are not viewable afterwards.
   - No UI can close an inspection.

4. **Packing.**
   - No screen or automatic path creates a packing order, and the empty-state copy wrongly says allocated sales orders create one.
   - Labels and barcodes exist only as data: the label endpoint is unused and nothing prints.
   - Cartons are never linked to dispatches: the UI sends `carton_ids: []`, and hand-over does not set `dispatches.packing_order_id`.
   - Assembly-to-packing hand-over has no UI.

5. **Dispatch UX.**
   - No edit after creation (PATCH is unused).
   - The gate-time LR, vehicle and tracking fields on the Dispatch action are unused.
   - The actual delivery date is always today.
   - Outbound QC_COMPLETED and GRN_COMPLETED cannot be reached from the UI.
   - The outbound tracking board's QC and GRN "pending" flags come from manually typed statuses, not real inspections or GRNs.
   - The DISPATCH_DELAYED notification links to `/dispatch/delayed`, which is not a page (B4 fixes this). The beat comment says it covers purchase orders, but it scans only outbound dispatches.

6. **Infrastructure and latent issues.**
   - In the base and dev compose files the Celery worker ignores the `reports` queue, so packing-list PDFs never render outside the prod overlay (A2 fixes this).
   - API-only latent defect: a GRN line posted with `location_id` holds stock at a bin, while the QC decision releases at the bin-less position, so the decision is refused (A3 only investigates).
   - Until C1a's allow-list gate lands, vendor roles (VENDOR_OWNER, VENDOR_DISPATCH_MANAGER) hold `dispatch.create` and `dispatch.update` (C:/Project/Other/ATCRAFT/apps/api/src/core/permissions.py L612-655), so a vendor user can see and raise company outbound dispatches.

**A06/A07 are about vendor shipments (inbound).**
- Outbound customer dispatches already capture all 12 transport fields, but only at creation, with no attachments and no immediate notifications.
- Inbound on main has only courier name, tracking reference and shipped date on the purchase order, writable through the API alone. There is no UI form, no notification, no board, and no inbound delay alert.
- C1a, C2a, C2b, B4 and D3 cover nearly all of it. Gaps left in the plan:
  - Staff cannot enter a full shipment on a vendor's behalf (staff get GET only).
  - Vendor-uploaded documents are not shown to staff on the PO detail or the inbound board.
  - Shipment notifications do not include ADMIN users and cannot say "LR copy uploaded".
  - Outbound attachments (LR copy, dispatch photo, POD) are not planned.
  - The purchase order's own status still sticks at QC_PENDING.

**No work package covers:** In-process, Final, Job-work and Assembly QC gaps; rework tracking; photo viewing; packing-order creation; label printing; carton tracking; dispatch planning and editing; the LR-copy attachment.

items.evidence: Charges accrue on job-work receipts (estimate_charges and receipt_charge in job_work/service.py; JobWorkOrder.total_charges and vendor_debit_amount). They are shown per order on /job-work (apps/web/src/features/job-work/job-work-page.tsx:405-437). GET /job-work/charges (finance.view or job_work.view, job_work/router.py:150-186) returns per-vendor period totals, but nothing calls it: it appears only in types/openapi.ts. A job worker's bill is a generic vendor invoice with no PO, so the match flags 'not linked to a purchase order' (finance/service.py:739), it can only be approved with an override, and it posts to PURCHASE_EXPENSE. Inventory: _build_receipt_movements (job_work/service.py:1807-1920) posts JOB_WORK_RECEIPT output with no unit_cost, so the output is valued at the item's standard cost (inventory/service.py:714-741, inbound_unit_cost fallback). Neither the processing charge nor the input material cost reaches the output's stock value.
items.gap: There is no job-work invoice or expense account, no billed-vs-accrued tracking, and no screen for the job-work cost summary. Processing cost is never capitalised into the output stock value.
items.planned_wp: B3a-job-work-invoice: typed JOB_WORK vendor invoice matched to receipt lines, JOB_WORK_EXPENSE account, invoiced_amount and billed-vs-unbilled tracking, excess-loss recovery journal, billable-lines endpoint, and an Invoices tab. B1 adds job_work_orders.cost_centre_id. Not covered: capitalising job-work cost into output inventory value, and a job-work cost report screen.
items.recommendation: Medium. On receipt, post JOB_WORK_RECEIPT with unit_cost = (FIFO value of the input consumed + receipt charge) / good output quantity. Alternatively, revalue on invoice approval. Add a JOB_WORK_COST report (vendor, process, order, input cost, charges, debits, cost per unit) and a Costs tab over /job-work/charges.

items.evidence: Per-job actual costing exists. GET /production/{order_id}/cost (production_cost.view, production/router.py:826-845) calls production_cost/_compute_cost (production/service.py:3326-3400). Material is costed at movement value and operations at actual time x work-centre rate, plus setup and process cost; the figures are frozen at close. They appear on the Costing tab of apps/web/src/features/production/production-detail-page.tsx (:746, tabs at :778). Missing finance integration: finished goods are received at standard cost and never revalued. The explicit ASSUMPTION at production/service.py:3004-3009 says 'revaluing finished stock from standard to actual is a finance function this module does not own', and no revaluation code exists anywhere. Nothing posts production cost or variance to the ledger. No ReportKey covers production cost across orders, and the production list shows no cost.
items.gap: Actual cost never flows into inventory value or the GL. There is no standard-vs-actual variance and no production-cost report by item, period or work centre.
items.planned_wp: none (B1 only tags production_orders.cost_centre_id. Its COST_CENTRE_EXPENSE report reads ledger_entries, which production never writes.)
items.recommendation: Medium to large. At close, revalue the job's receipts still on hand to actual cost, or post an actual-cost unit_cost / variance movement. Add a PRODUCTION_COST report (order, item, quantity, material, operation, total, per unit, standard vs actual variance; filters for period, work centre and cost centre). Add WIP/variance journals only if inventory accounts are introduced.

items.evidence: GET /finance/outstanding (finance.view, finance/router.py:706-745) calls list_outstanding (service.py:3424), which reads VendorInvoiceRepository.outstanding_stmt (repository.py:991). One is GET /finance/ageing?party_type=CUSTOMER (router.py:748-804), which ages from the posting date (repository.py:549-746), so not_due is always 0 and customers.credit_days is unused. items.evidence: GET /finance/gst-summary (gst_report.view, finance/router.py:865-884) calls gst_summary (service.py:3758-3790). The GST summary tab (apps/web/src/features/finance/gst-summary-tab.tsx) shows output, input and net per HSN and rate. Output tax is derived from dispatches x the SO line's tax share (GstRepository.output_rows_stmt, repository.py:1707-1764) and grouped by today's Item.hsn_code. No application code posts OUTPUT_TAX, so the ledger and the report disagree. Customer credits and purchase returns are not netted. There is no invoice-wise (GSTIN-wise) listing and no export.
items.gap: The report is not invoice-based. HSN codes are not snapshotted. Credit notes and purchase-return debit notes are not netted. There are no GSTR-1/3B-style sections or export.
items.planned_wp: A2-sales-invoice: output from issued invoice lines with the HSN snapshot, a dispatched-not-invoiced figure, and OUTPUT_TAX posted. A3-returns-credit-notes: credit notes subtracted. Not covered: input-tax reversal for purchase returns/debit notes, and a GSTR-1 invoice-wise listing with export.
items.recommendation: Medium, after A2 and A3. Deduct vendor debit notes from input tax. Add GSTR-1 sections (B2B invoice-wise with buyer GSTIN/POS, B2C summary, CDNR from credit notes, HSN summary) and a GSTR-3B summary, exported as XLSX through the reports job pipeline.

Cost is quantity x today's manually entered Item.standard_cost (repository.py:788), not the FIFO cost actually dispatched and not actual production cost. notes:
Scope and basis. This is a read-only audit of main at HEAD cdac4e0; no lane branch is merged, so every PLANNED status depends on WPs in rounds 1-5 landing. Paths are relative to C:\Project\Other\ATCRAFT. Every report under /reports is served by the generic runner apps/web/src/features/reports/reports-page.tsx (route /reports, permission report.view, populated from GET /reports/catalogue). That is the screen evidence for each PRESENT report.

1. The GL is minimal. The default chart (finance/service.py:477-492) has no revenue, sales-returns, inventory, WIP, COGS, job-work-expense or freight account. Only vendor invoices, payments and customer adjustments post journals. Dispatch, production, job-work receipts and purchase returns post nothing, and OUTPUT_TAX is never posted by application code, so the GST report and the ledger disagree until A2. No route shows one account's ledger or a trial balance, even though ix_ledger_entries_account_date exists. A GL account statement plus a trial balance (small to medium, not in any WP) would close the 'Sales ledger' and 'Purchase ledger' gaps once A2 lands.

2. Defects found that affect the ledgers:
   - Vendor-invoice cancel after a dispute (APPROVED->DISPUTED->CANCELLED, finance/service.py:2357-2389) does not reverse the posted journal. B3a fixes it; make sure it lands before the vendor and purchase ledgers are trusted.
   - Purchase returns post no debit note and no GST input reversal. No WP covers this, and it affects P13.M2, M3 and M9.

3. Actual cost never reaches inventory or finance:
   - Production receipts are valued at standard cost by explicit ASSUMPTION (production/service.py:3004-3009), and nothing ever revalues them.
   - Job-work outputs carry no unit_cost (job_work/service.py:1807-1920).
   - Product profitability uses the current manual standard_cost against booked orders.
   - No WP addresses P13.M6, P14.11, or the capitalisation part of P13.M5.

4. Report authorisation. Every /reports route needs only report.view, and /reports/catalogue is not filtered per user, despite the comment at reports-page.tsx:4. SALES_EXECUTIVE holds report.view but not item.cost_view or inventory.valuation_view, yet sees product cost and margin plus stock values (inventory-valuation, and valuation_amount on stock-availability and dead-stock). Recommend per-report permissions with catalogue filtering (small).

5. Dashboard defect. The 'POs awaiting approval' tile (dashboard-page.tsx:225-236) shows POs awaiting delivery (APPROVED/SENT/ACKNOWLEDGED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED). It is not planned to be fixed.

6. Machine-utilisation defect. Machines with no finished work order in the period are omitted, because the query starts from work_orders (reports/repository.py:1066-1078). B2 does not fix it.

7. Report UX gaps:
   - There is no XLSX/PDF export for results under 5000 rows; export only exists past the inline limit.
   - The UI offers no category filter (reports-page.tsx:120-122).
   - Period reports filter on one date column with a 366-day cap, so long-overdue items outside the chosen period are missed (purchase-pending by po_date, job-work-pending by expected_return_date).

8. A09 dispatch reports. In the proposal these concern vendor (inbound) shipments. Today's courier-tracking, dispatch and vendor-dispatch-history reports are outbound only; vendor-dispatch-history lists our dispatches to vendors. Inbound coverage depends on the chain C0 (PO category) -> C1a (purchase_order_shipments, inbound board API) -> C2b (board page) -> B5 (reports, round 5). Small outbound gaps that no WP covers: an expected-today filter, a courier filter on courier-tracking, and freight totals per transporter.

9. Security observed in passing. Vendor-role users can currently read /finance/ledger/customer/{any} and /finance/ledger/vendor/{any}, because finance has no vendor scoping and the vendor presets hold ledger.view. C1a's allow-list gate closes this.

10. The sales lifecycle never reaches INVOICED or CLOSED (no caller). A2 adds invoicing and POST /sales/{id}/close.

notes:
I audited the main tree only: C:\Project\Other\ATCRAFT, branch main, HEAD cdac4e0. None of the lane work packages are merged yet, so every PLANNED_* status depends on rounds 1-5 landing. Paths in the evidence are relative to that root.

Cross-cutting findings, each checked in code:

1. **Notifications barely fire.** Only 4 of the 20 NotificationType members are ever raised: REPORT_READY, DISPATCH_DELAYED, QC_FAILED and ALLOCATION_CHANGED. Three of the four have unusable links:
   - '/dispatch/delayed' is not a SPA route; the working page is /dispatch?tab=tracking&delayed_only=true.
   - '/allocation/reservations/{id}' is not a route either.
   - REPORT_READY links to the API path /api/v1/reports/jobs/{id}.
   - QC_FAILED has no link at all.

   The dispatch delay alert also re-fires every hour once it is read, because delay_notified_at is written but never read. Nothing anywhere targets vendor users. notify_role with a vendor role code would reach every vendor in the company.

2. **Vendor security holes.**
   - The vendor role presets grant dispatch.*, vendor_invoice.*, payment.view, ledger.view, job_work.view, qc.view and document.* on modules that apply no vendor scope. A vendor login can read every customer's dispatches and every vendor's invoices and payments, and can create invoices for any vendor_id.
   - POST /procurement/purchase-orders/check-duplicates leaks other vendors' open POs.
   - Vendors see their own DRAFT and PENDING_APPROVAL POs.

   No demo vendor users exist, but /admin/users can create them today. C1a P0 and C0 §9/§11 must ship before any vendor account is issued.

3. **Trap T7 is fixed by no work package.**
   - quality decide_inspection never updates GRN line qc_status (it is set only at procurement/service.py:2863-2866, 3162 and 3247).
   - So a PO whose lines needed QC stays in QC_PENDING for ever, and the TrackingPanel shows qc_pending=true for ever.
   - INVOICED and PAID are never set on a PO.

   C1a and B4 deliberately route around this, but the PO status the staff screen shows, and the vendor app will show, stays wrong. It needs a small fix: a procurement port called from decide_inspection.

4. **The generic approvals queue is empty.** approval_requests (audit/models.py:113) is never written by anything in src. The dashboard panel 'Approvals waiting for me' (GET /audit/approvals) is therefore always empty, and GET /procurement/pending-approvals has no screen. This compounds the A01.M10 gap.

5. **Job-work vendors get nothing.** C1a's allow-list gate removes vendors' current (insecure) job-work access and gives job-work vendors no portal replacement. No work package covers 'Job work pending' for the vendor (A01.M8).

6. **Delivery-channel assumptions to confirm with Atcraft.**
   - Push and the vendor/dealer 'mobile app' are planned as an installable PWA with Web Push: Android Chrome, and iOS 16.4+ only after Add to Home Screen. No store app is planned.
   - WhatsApp/SMS (D2) and the courier API (D3) stay inert until Atcraft provides accounts: a Meta WhatsApp Business account with approved templates, a DLT-registered SMS sender and templates, and Shiprocket credentials.
   - D4's signature is app-level Ed25519, not a CA-issued DSC.

7. **Types still unraised after every work package:** PRODUCTION_ORDER_DELAYED, SALES_ORDER_AT_RISK, STOCK_BELOW_REORDER, BACKGROUND_JOB_COMPLETED/FAILED and SYSTEM_ANNOUNCEMENT. They are not in the proposal's lists, but the Preferences screen offers them. Either raise them (the reorder and production delay sweeps are small) or hide them.

8. **Small issues in what exists.**
   - The frontend NOTIFICATION_TYPES list (notification-types.ts:27-48) is a hand-maintained copy of the enum; B4 adds a guard test for it.
   - The beat comment at celery_app.py:85-86 wrongly claims purchase-order delay alerts.
   - E-mail has no recovery sweep for lost publishes; C1b adds one.

9. **Recipient gaps that remain after the specs** (the PLANNED_PARTIAL rows):
   - B4 sends 'Dispatch created' and outbound 'Courier tracking updated' only to the customer's optional assigned sales user, with no fallback.
   - No spec notifies the buyer about inbound shipment updates after creation, or about delivery.
   - B4's vendor-invoice-pending rule ignores partially received POs.

   All are small fixes inside B4.

items.item: Direct finished-goods sale. Dealer orders 100 handles; FG stock is checked, reserved and dispatched.
items.evidence: Backend chain works via API: POST /sales (sales_order.create) -> POST /sales/{id}/confirm (sales_order.update; sales/service.py:1608 confirm_order reads free stock at the order warehouse via AvailabilityRepository.available_by_item :1667, takes a HARD reservation through allocation.reserve :1679, and walks CONFIRMED->ALLOCATED when fully covered :1704-1719) -> POST /dispatch, /dispatch/{id}/ready, /dispatch/{id}/dispatch (dispatch.create/update; dispatch/service.py:1390 dispatch_consignment consumes order_line.reservation_id via allocation.consume and posts DISPATCH, then walks ALLOCATED->PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED->DISPATCHED). This is proven only with lines that carry sales_order_line_id: tests/integration/test_dispatch_service.py:318 and core/demo_data/operations.py:2399. Screens: sales-orders-page.tsx, sales-order-detail-page.tsx (Confirm action and Allocation panel), dispatch-page.tsx with dispatch-dialogs.tsx (create, ready, dispatch). Dealers are customers of type DEALER.
items.gap: The dispatch screen never links a line to a sales-order line. LineEditor (dispatch-dialogs.tsx:111-187) sends only item, quantity, batch and serials, and nothing in apps/web sets sales_order_line_id. The backend does not auto-match lines either (_validate_lines/_persist_lines, dispatch/service.py:696-875). dispatch_consignment therefore treats every UI line as unreserved (:1491-1538) and posts a plain DISPATCH from AVAILABLE. The inventory engine refuses that when the only stock is the stock reserved for this order (inventory/service.py:1158, 'reserved' shortfall), which is exactly the K01 case. When surplus free stock exists, it ships the free stock instead: the order's 100 stay reserved, sales_order_lines.dispatched_quantity stays 0, and the header is still walked to PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED (open_line_count, dispatch/repository.py:460). The dialog text at dispatch-dialogs.tsx:266 and :373 promises a reservation consumption that does not happen. The sales order detail page has no Dispatch action. Invoice and close after dispatch are covered by A2.
items.planned_wp: none (A2 builds invoice lines from dispatch lines carrying sales_order_line_id, so A2 depends on this fix; C3a/C4a add dealer self-ordering, not this)
items.recommendation: Small/medium. (1) In CreateDispatchDialog, when a sales order is chosen, load GET /sales/{id}/allocation-status and pre-fill one line per open SO line with sales_order_line_id, item and quantity = min(reserved, outstanding), editable downward only. (2) Server-side, when a SALES dispatch names sales_order_id, require every line to carry sales_order_line_id (or auto-match by item when unambiguous) and refuse otherwise. (3) Add a 'Dispatch' action on sales-order-detail-page.tsx that opens the pre-filled dialog. (4) Add a vitest asserting the POST body carries sales_order_line_id, an API test showing a UI-shaped payload consumes the reservation, and an e2e journey SO -> confirm -> dispatch.

items.item: Finished goods not available. Dealer orders 500 handles with only 120 available; the system allocates 120 and generates a production plan for the remaining 380.
items.evidence: Allocating the 120 works: confirm_order reserves min(demand, free) per line (sales/service.py:1675-1702, reservable_quantity :409) and returns the per-line shortfall (router message 'N line(s) short of stock', sales/router.py:246-250). GET /sales/{id}/allocation-status shows Reserved, Shortfall and Free stock (sales-order-detail-page.tsx AllocationPanel :85-240). Planning is manual: the panel only offers a link, 'Run MRP to plan the balance' -> /mrp (:207-223). A planner must run POST /mrp/runs (mrp.run; mrp-page.tsx). The run plans open SO demand net of reservations (mrp/repository.py:138-213, open quantity = qty - dispatched - allocated) and emits a MANUFACTURE suggestion for MAKE items (mrp/engine.py:728-760). The planner then converts it via POST /mrp/suggestions/{id}/convert (mrp.convert_suggestion; mrp-run-detail-page.tsx), which calls production.create_order_from_mrp (production/service.py:1219) and creates a DRAFT production order with source MRP_SUGGESTION.
items.gap: Nothing generates a production plan when the order is confirmed. There is no hook, event or task after confirm_order, and the Celery beat schedule has no MRP job. ProductionSourceType.SALES_ORDER exists (production/models.py:134) but nothing ever creates a production order with it. The plan therefore needs two manual planner steps plus approval, and the resulting production order is not tied to the sales order. Worse, the order can never ship even after the 380 are made. It stays CONFIRMED for good: CONFIRMED->ALLOCATED happens only inside confirm_order when every line is fully covered (sales/service.py:1709-1719), and _update_confirmed never transitions. Dispatch accepts only ALLOCATED or PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED (dispatch/service.py:440-464).
items.planned_wp: none (B4 only adds a 'Production shortage' notification after an MRP run completes)
items.recommendation: Medium. (1) On confirm with a shortfall, behind a setting such as AUTO_PLAN_ON_CONFIRM, create in the same transaction a DRAFT production order (source_type SALES_ORDER, source id plus line id, quantity = shortfall net of open supply) for MAKE items or MAKE_OR_BUY items with a default BOM, and a DRAFT purchase requisition for BUY items. Alternatively, enqueue a scoped MRP run (Celery) that auto-converts. (2) Add a 'Plan shortfall' button to the allocation panel. (3) Add the allocation top-up described under K08, so production output is reserved for the order and the order moves CONFIRMED->ALLOCATED once covered.

items.item: Urgent order reallocation. Parts reserved for future production are needed by an urgent dealer order; the system suggests reallocation with approval.
items.evidence: The engine is present. suggest_reallocation ranks donor reservations under a configurable ReallocationPolicy: priority gap, date slack, SOFT bonus, untouched bonus and protect_within_days (allocation/service.py:257-330, :1258). POST /allocation/reallocation-requests (allocation.reallocate) raises a PENDING request against the best donor. POST /allocation/reallocation-requests/{id}/approve and /reject (allocation.approve, separate approver enforced at :1783) execute release plus reserve in one transaction and notify the donor (:1335-1581). Production holds HARD component reservations (production/service.py:1488-1500). UI: the 'Suggest reallocation' dialog in reservations-page.tsx (:677-940, :1127-1134).
items.gap: (1) No screen lists, approves or rejects reallocation requests. GET /allocation/reallocation-requests, /approve and /reject are called nowhere in apps/web, and no approval_requests row is written, so the dashboard approval queue never shows them either. Approval is API-only. (2) A request can only be raised from an existing reservation row of the recipient. An urgent order that got nothing reserved (all stock held by production) has no row to start from, and the sales order screen has no such action. Nothing suggests reallocation automatically when a short or urgent order is confirmed: suggest_reallocation has no other caller, and is_urgent is never read by allocation. (3) Executing creates the recipient reservation with demand_line_id=None (allocation/service.py:1440) and never updates sales_order_lines.allocated_quantity, reservation_id or status, nor the order status. The urgent order therefore still shows the shortfall and stays CONFIRMED, so it cannot be dispatched. Dispatch also cannot consume the reallocated reservation, because it only consumes order_line.reservation_id (dispatch/service.py:1496).
items.planned_wp: none (B4 only adds a 'Stock reallocation request' notification to allocation.approve holders and fixes the donor notification link)
items.recommendation: Medium. (1) Add a Reallocation requests page or tab: GET ...?status=PENDING with Approve and Reject gated on P.ALLOCATION_APPROVE, or write approval_requests rows so requests reach the dashboard queue. (2) Add 'Request reallocation' to the SO allocation panel for short lines, pre-filling to_demand SALES_ORDER plus the line, quantity = shortfall and priority from the order. (3) Add to_demand_line_id to reallocation_requests. On execute, link the new reservation to the SO line (merge into reservation_id, raise allocated_quantity, recompute the line status) and move CONFIRMED->ALLOCATED when the order is covered. (4) Optionally, auto-suggest donors when an urgent order confirms short, and map is_urgent to a priority.

items.item: Packing material shortage. The finished product is ready but the box is unavailable; the system creates a purchase request for packing material.
items.evidence: Packing consumes packing material: seal_carton posts a MATERIAL_ISSUE for the carton's box item (packing/service.py:1534-1605; POST /packing/{order_id}/cartons/{carton_id}/seal), so a missing box surfaces as InsufficientStockError. packing-order-dialog.tsx:331-352 lists the boxes with their free quantity and warns 'No packing material is in stock at this warehouse...'. Manual remedies exist: the 'Below reorder level' filter on balances-page.tsx, POST /procurement/purchase-requisitions (requisitions-page.tsx), and manual demand lines in an MRP run.
items.gap: Nothing creates a purchase request for packing material. The packing module never calls procurement. There is no packing-material requirement per packing order or per item (no packing specification). There is no reorder-level sweep: PurchaseSourceType.REORDER is defined (procurement/models.py:260) but no code uses it. MRP plans a box only when it is a BOM component of something being manufactured, which does not apply here because the finished goods are already made.
items.recommendation: Medium. (1) Add a packing specification per sellable item (box item, units per carton), or derive the box requirement from the packing order. (2) On packing-order create or start, compare the box requirement with free stock. When short, create a DRAFT purchase requisition in the same transaction (new source_type PACKING_ORDER, or REORDER), deduplicated against open requisitions and POs for the item, and notify purchase. (3) Add a daily Celery sweep that raises requisitions for PACKING_MATERIAL items below reorder_level. (4) Show 'requisition PR/... raised' on the packing screen.

items.item: Job work vendor process. Material goes to a vendor for coating; sent, received, rejected and pending quantities are tracked.
items.evidence: The process works end to end. JobWorkProcess has COATING (job_work/models.py:92-108). Routes POST /job-work, /{id}/approve, /{id}/issue (challan plus JOB_WORK_ISSUE movement), /{id}/receive, /{id}/qc-result and /{id}/close carry job_work.* and qc.decide permissions (job_work/router.py:208-460). JobWorkOrderLine tracks issued_quantity, received_quantity, received_output_quantity, rejected_quantity and scrap_quantity (models.py:395-435), alongside inventory_balances.job_work_quantity. Read endpoints GET /job-work/pending-at-vendor and GET /job-work/{id}/reconciliation exist. Screens: job-work-page.tsx (Orders tab and 'Pending at vendor' tab :795) and job-work-dialogs.tsx (issue; receive with Received and Rejected inputs :401; QC result :700). The receive dialog shows 'Issued X - still at vendor Y'. The /reports page renders Job-work pending (GET /reports/job-work-pending), with issued, received and pending per order.
items.gap: Sent, received and pending quantities are visible, but the rejected quantity is only captured, never shown afterwards. There is no job-work order detail view: the list shows only the receipt count (job-work-page.tsx:387-402). No screen calls GET /job-work/{id}/reconciliation. JobWorkPendingRow (reports/schemas.py:207-220) has no rejected column.
items.planned_wp: none (B3a covers the job-work invoice, not this view)
items.recommendation: Small. Add a job-work order detail drawer or page on /job-work that renders the GET /job-work/{id} lines (issued, received output, rejected, scrap, still at vendor) and the reconciliation report. Add rejected_quantity and scrap_quantity to the JOB_WORK_PENDING report row.

items.item: Partial dispatch. A customer orders 500 with 200 available; the system dispatches 200 and plans the balance 300.
items.evidence: Partial dispatch of a fully allocated order works through the API: dispatch_balance and sales_order_status_path (dispatch/service.py:352-420) take the order ALLOCATED->PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED->DISPATCHED (tests/integration/test_dispatch_service.py:497, :516). The balance can be planned by a manual MRP run, since open demand excludes dispatched and reserved quantities (mrp/repository.py:161-166).
items.gap: The scenario itself is refused. Confirming 500 with 200 free leaves the order CONFIRMED (sales/service.py:1708-1719). assert_order_dispatchable accepts only ALLOCATED or PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED (dispatch/service.py:440-464, pinned by tests/unit/test_dispatch_lifecycle.py:265-303), so the 200 cannot ship: the error says 'must be fully allocated before a consignment can leave'. Nothing ever moves CONFIRMED->ALLOCATED later. There is no top-up or re-allocate endpoint, _update_confirmed re-reserves but never transitions, and reallocation does not touch the sales order. Planning the balance is not automatic (see K02). Through the UI the dispatch would also hit the unlinked-line defect described under K01.
items.recommendation: Medium. (1) Let a partially allocated order ship what is reserved: add a CONFIRMED->PARTIALLY_DISPATCHED edge (the dispatchable set derives from the state machine, so it follows automatically) and cap each line's dispatch at its live reservation. (2) Add POST /sales/{id}/allocate (sales_order.update) that reserves newly free stock for short lines by priority and moves CONFIRMED->ALLOCATED when covered. Also top up automatically when stock arrives: GRN post, production or assembly output, transfer receipt. (3) Plan the balance automatically as in K02. (4) Update the unit test that pins the gate, and add an e2e for the 500/200 case.

items.item: Quality rejection. Received material fails QC; the system moves it to rejected stock and starts a vendor return / replacement process.
items.evidence: Posting a GRN raises an INCOMING inspection and holds the stock in QC_HOLD (procurement/service.py:3246-3247). POST /quality/inspections/{id}/decide (qc.decide) moves the rejected quantity QC_HOLD->DAMAGED through change_stock_state (quality/service.py:1705-1706) and sets return_required (:1825). It also sends a CRITICAL QC_FAILED notification: 'Vendor return owed... Raise a purchase return or agree a replacement' (:1965-1985). quality-page.tsx shows a 'To vendor' badge (:410-418). A purchase return can be raised by hand from the GRN and draws from the DAMAGED pool (procurement/models.py:241 RETURNABLE_STOCK_STATES and :1467; POST /procurement/purchase-returns and /{id}/post with purchase_return.create; purchase-returns-page.tsx and purchase-return-dialogs.tsx).
items.gap: Nothing starts the return or the replacement. Quality deliberately only flags the lot (ASSUMPTION at quality/service.py:77-81 and :1821-1825). No draft purchase return is created, and the inspection has no 'Raise return' action. return_required is never linked to a return, nor cleared when one is posted. There is no replacement path at all: PurchaseReturn has only DRAFT, POSTED and CANCELLED, with no CREDIT vs REPLACEMENT resolution and no replacement PO or expected re-receipt. Rejected stock stays in the DAMAGED pool of the same warehouse rather than moving to a rejection store, which is acceptable but should be stated.
items.planned_wp: none for the return itself (C1a/C2a add only vendor-portal visibility of QC results and a vendor-facing QC_FAILED notification)
items.recommendation: Medium. (1) On a REJECTED incoming decision against a vendor, create a DRAFT purchase return in the same transaction (lines from the GRN line, stock_state DAMAGED, quantity = rejected, reason from the inspection), or at minimum add a 'Raise return' button that pre-fills it. (2) Add resolution_type (CREDIT_NOTE or REPLACEMENT) to purchase_returns. For REPLACEMENT, re-open the PO line's pending quantity or add a replacement PO line, so the replacement is expected and received against the PO. (3) Link the inspection to the return and clear return_required when the return is posted. (4) Show open-return status on the quality and GRN screens.

items.item: Multi-warehouse allocation. If one warehouse is short, the system checks another and suggests a stock transfer.
items.evidence: Multi-warehouse stock and manual transfers exist. Balances are kept per warehouse (balances-page.tsx). Stock transfers run through POST /inventory/transfers, /{id}/approve, /dispatch, /receive and /cancel (inventory.transfer; inventory/router.py:411-530; movements-page.tsx:285-412; movement-dialogs.tsx:271). GET /allocation/available-to-promise without warehouse_id sums stock across all warehouses. MrpSuggestionType.TRANSFER exists in the vocabulary.
items.gap: Confirmation and allocation look only at the order's own warehouse: sales/service.py:1667 calls available_by_item(item_ids, order.warehouse_id), and the 'Free stock' figure in allocation-status does the same (:936). Nothing checks other warehouses or suggests a transfer. The MRP engine never produces TRANSFER suggestions, as mrp/models.py:129-137 says outright, although mrp-run-detail-page.tsx has UI text for them. Transfers carry no link to the demand they serve.
items.recommendation: Medium. (1) Add an availability-by-warehouse read (one grouped query) to confirm and allocation-status that returns transfer suggestions (source warehouse, quantity) for short lines. (2) On the SO allocation panel, show 'Available elsewhere' with a 'Raise transfer' action that pre-fills POST /inventory/transfers with a source reference to the order, optionally taking a SOFT reservation at the source warehouse. (3) Optionally, add an MRP warehouse-balancing pass that produces TRANSFER suggestions, with a conversion hook into inventory transfers.
